title: Lee Roy Selmon: OU Legend Who Became USF's Athletic Director
question: What did Lee Roy Selmon do after his NFL career?
answer: Lee Roy Selmon, an OU defensive lineman from 1972 to 1975, became USF's athletic director in 2001 and opened Lee Roy Selmon's restaurant in Tampa in 2000.
summary: Lee Roy Selmon (OU 1972-75) became a Pro Football Hall of Famer, then served as USF's athletic director and opened a namesake restaurant in Tampa in 2000.
body: Lee Roy Selmon grew up outside Eufaula and followed his older brother Lucious to Norman, where he and brother Dewey were good enough to play varsity football as freshmen. Lee Roy played for the Sooners from 1972 through 1975, earning All-America honors on the 1974 and 1975 national championship teams. As a senior in 1975, he won both the Outland Trophy and the Lombardi Award.

The expansion Tampa Bay Buccaneers made him the first draft pick in franchise history in 1976. He became the face of their defense, was the unanimous NFL Defensive Player of the Year in 1979 and made six straight Pro Bowls. He entered the Pro Football Hall of Fame in 1995, the first former Sooner to do so.

Selmon stayed in Tampa after football and became a pillar of the community. He joined the University of South Florida in 1993 as an associate athletic director and was promoted to athletic director in 2001.

He also went into the restaurant business, opening Lee Roy Selmon's in Tampa in 2000. The family had a barbecue tradition, too: in 1988 the Selmon brothers began marketing Selmon Brothers Fine Bar-B-Q Sauce, built on a recipe brother Charles used at his restaurant in Wichita. Tampa honored Lee Roy by naming an expressway after him.
Selmon died in September 2011, but in Oklahoma and Florida alike he is remembered as one of the most respected men ever to dominate a football field.
